Subject: SIG questionnaire — next steps and acceptance criteria

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the quick demo yesterday. Procurement asked us to get an updated SIG (Std Info Gathering) and a short summary of acceptance criteria for privacy items — specifically: DPA, SCC applicability, and whether Redwood is willing/able to execute a BAA for HIPAA-covered data.

Can you send: 
- A high-level acceptance checklist (what would need to be in place for MedAlliance legal to sign the DPA/SCCs)
- Any callouts where a BAA would be infeasible or would require a private deployment
- A short evidence pack (SOC2 summary, system diagrams, and any artifacts that would help our privacy/legal team triage)

We'd appreciate a target date — Procurement is aiming to finalize vendor short-listing by Dec 7.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — next steps and acceptance criteria

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. I pulled together a proposed approach and an initial evidence bundle (attached). High-level notes below, and I copied the internal leads for privacy, security, and legal to make sure answers are complete.

Quick summary:
- DPA/SCCs: Redwood supports DPAs and can provide SCC-compliant transfer mechanisms (we rely on standard EU SCCs for transfers from EU; for US-based MedAlliance the DPA is straightforward).
- BAA/HIPAA: Redwood can support HIPAA-covered workloads under our Redwood Private offering or via a Dedicated plan with a signed BAA. Hosted/shared API (standard hosted tier) is not suitable for regulated PHI without Private/Dedicated controls.
- Acceptance checklist (short):
  1) Executed DPA referencing SCCs if cross-border transfers are needed;
  2) If PHI is in scope: an executed BAA + Private/Dedicated deployment (customer-managed keys optional but recommended);
  3) SOC 2 Type II report in-scope for relevant control categories (we included a one-page summary);
  4) Network diagram and encryption-at-rest/key management description;
  5) Evidence of retention/deletion policies and audit logging.

Attached: redwood_SIG_partial_answers_v1.xlsx, SOC2-summary-2025.pdf, network-diagram.png, hipaa-feasibility-brief.docx

Proposed timeline:
- Today (Nov 29): deliver partial SIG answers + evidence (attached)
- Dec 1: internal deep-dive with MedAlliance privacy/legal (if helpful)
- Dec 4: final answers and any tailored contract language for DPA/BAA

Ben and Priyom — can you confirm the secure deployment/keys wording for the BAA note and whether we should propose a private instance SLA? Neha/Rishi — any legal caveats to call out on SCCs and DPA language?

Best,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — next steps and acceptance criteria

Laura — quick notes from GTM/security lens: 

- For Sales: emphasize Dedicated vs Private trade-offs. Dedicated (single-tenant GPU pool + committed capacity) is usually acceptable for customers wanting PHI without full private air-gap. Private (VPC/on-prem) is our recommended route for highest assurance and when customer requires customer-managed networking/KMS.
- Pricing: if they go Private we should prepare an indicative uplift (typical range + rough timeline).
- For Procurement deadline (Dec 7) we should commit to the Dec 4 final answers. If they ask for faster, we can escalate but need legal sign-off on contract language.

Prio: confirm whether we can propose a templated BAA and add a note on key management options.

Ben
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-11-29T13:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire — next steps and acceptance criteria

Laura/Ben —

Couple of technical clarifications for the evidence pack and the acceptance checklist: 

1) BAA feasibility: we can sign BAAs when the workload is hosted on Dedicated or Private. For Hosted API (shared), we do not sign BAAs. Note that for Dedicated we still manage the control plane unless customer wants Private. I recommend: "BAA possible w/ Dedicated or Private; Private preferred for network isolation and customer-managed KMS."

2) SCCs: we support standard SCC mechanisms. For EU-origin data transferring to US control plane customers should expect SCC appendix in DPA. If MedAlliance insists on EU-only residency, Private with region pinning is required.

3) Evidence log: I'll prepare a short mapping (SIG question -> evidence artifact filename + page/section) to speed MedAlliance review. Targeting Dec 1 morning for that mapping and an internal review.

Attaching: hipaa-feasibility-brief.docx (internal draft)

Priyom
Security & Compliance

Hi Elena —

Following up with the deliverables we discussed. Attached is a partial SIG worksheet with question-level answers (redwood_SIG_partial_answers_v1.xlsx). Priyom provided a mapping doc that ties each SIG item to a supporting artifact; Ben included a short note on procurement/pricing posture.

Key highlights: 
- BAA: possible when workload is on Dedicated or Private. For clarity we've summarized the trade-offs in the attached hipaa-feasibility-brief.docx (see section "When BAA is feasible").
- SCC/DPA: we will include SCC annex if EU jurisdictions are in scope. DPA redlines we typically accept are limited to data processing scope, retention, and standard liability caps.
- Evidence pack (zip list): SOC2-summary-2025.pdf (control summary), network-diagram.png (logical architecture), hipaa-feasibility-brief.docx, redwood_SIG_partial_answers_v1.xlsx.

Next steps we propose:
1) Confirm whether PHI will be in scope (simple yes/no). If yes, we recommend a short technical call between MedAlliance infra/security and Redwood SecOps to scope Dedicated vs Private.
2) We will send final SIG answers + evidence mapping by Dec 4.

Can you confirm the PHI scope by EOD Dec 2 so we can lock resources?

Thanks,
Laura

Jordan/Elena —

Answers inline and final bundle plan: 

- Dedicated contractual addendum: No separate subscription is strictly required, but Dedicated deployments include a capacity commitment and a modest uplift. If you proceed we will include a short SOW addendum to the base agreement that captures capacity, region, and SLA metrics. The BAA will be a standalone annex executed alongside the DPA/contract.

- SOC2 Type II: we can provide a redacted SOC2 Type II (full report is shared under NDA). Attached to this thread is the redacted SOC2 (SOC2-redacted-2025.pdf).

- Final evidence bundle (one-line items):
  • Redacted SOC2 Type II (controls summary) — SOC2-redacted-2025.pdf
  • SIG worksheet (question-level answers) — redwood_SIG_final_answers_v1.xlsx
  • Evidence mapping (SIG question -> artifact) — evidence-mapping-dec03.csv
  • Network diagram (logical architecture) — network-diagram.png
  • HIPAA feasibility brief (includes BAA path) — hipaa-feasibility-brief.docx
  • Sample BAA template (annotated) — BAA-template-redwood.docx

We will deliver the final bundle and the evidence mapping by EOD Dec 4 (we can also arrange a 30-min technical call Dec 5 if you'd like deeper scoping). Please confirm PHI-in-scope flag so we can prioritize the Private/Dedicated diagram details.

Thanks — and happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Laura
